delivered mixed
as rapid AI cloud growth returned its core business to year-over-year expansion, while advertising weakness,
iQIYI, Inc.
declines and continued AI investment pressured consolidated revenue and near-term profitability.
The stock slid 4% after the results, hitting a new 52-week low.
Revenue Slips, but Core Business Returns to Growth
Baidu generated 30.8 billion yuan ($4.595 billion) in third-quarter revenue, down 1% year over year and 2% sequentially, slightly below the
of $4.610 billion. Baidu General Business revenue rose 1% to 25.0 billion yuan, while iQIYI revenue fell 10% to 6.0 billion yuan.
Baidu Core AI-powered businesses generated 13.2 billion yuan, accounting for 53% of Baidu general business revenue, as AI-related operations continued to take a larger share of the company’s mix.
AI Cloud Becomes the Main Growth Engine

AI Cloud Infra revenue jumped 94% year over year, accelerating from 50% growth in the previous quarter. GPU Cloud revenue rose 191% year over year and about 43% sequentially, while external customers’ token-usage revenue on the Qianfan MaaS platform increased more than 12-fold.
CEO
Robin Li
said AI Cloud Infra is becoming "a key driver of Baidu’s overall revenue growth," supported by Baidu’s full-stack capabilities across chips, cloud infrastructure, models and applications.
EVP
Dou Shen

said demand remains strong across both training and inference, with inference still in the early stages of scaling. He also pointed to broader adoption across e-commerce, internet, autonomous driving and embodied AI.
Longer Contracts Improve Visibility and Cash Recovery
Baidu said customers are committing to longer GPU Cloud contracts and making more prepayments to secure capacity.
Its three largest GPU Cloud customers by contract value all extended to multi-year agreements during renewals, including one customer that lengthened its contract term sixfold.
Management said those commitments improve revenue visibility, cash flow and payback periods on infrastructure investment.
Cloud Margins Improve As Mix Shifts Higher
AI Cloud Infra increased both profit and margins year over year and sequentially.

Management said GPU Cloud, Kunlunxin and MaaS now represent a majority of AI Cloud Infra revenue and carry better margins. Greater utilization, full-stack optimization and higher-value services should support further margin expansion over time.
Baidu’s adjusted operating margin declined to 6% from 7% a year ago.
Adjusted earnings of $1.01 per American depositary share beat the analyst consensus estimate of 71 cents.
Cash Flow Remains Positive
Baidu generated 2.8 billion yuan of operating cash flow, marking its fifth consecutive quarter of positive operating cash flow.
The company ended September with 276.6 billion yuan in cash and investments. CFO
Henry He
said Baidu will keep investing "with very strict discipline" and tie new spending to clear customer demand and attractive returns.
Baidu also reduced Q3 CapEx by 4 billion yuan sequentially, helped by earlier compute investments and better utilization of existing infrastructure.
ERNIE, Agents and AI Applications Expand
Baidu plans to accelerate development across the ERNIE family while keeping model development application-driven rather than chasing benchmark leadership alone.
Li said stronger in-house models should improve user experiences, reduce costs and support monetization, while Qianfan can extend ERNIE to external customers.
Its general work agent DuMate grew monthly active users more than 30-fold quarter over quarter in September, while Baidu also expanded Yijing, Famou and KOOKO across enterprise applications.
Apollo Go Expands Internationally
Apollo Go continued scaling autonomous ride-hailing operations.
Fully driverless rides in Shenzhen rose about 170% sequentially, while its Dubai fleet doubled. Baidu also expanded open-road testing in London with
Uber Technologies, Inc.
and
Lyft, Inc.
and continued fully driverless testing in Hong Kong. Apollo Go now operates across 30 cities.
Kunlunxin Adds Another Growth Avenue
Baidu continues to advance the proposed Hong Kong listing of Kunlunxin, its in-house AI chip business.

The company expects the M100 inference chip to enter volume production soon and plans to introduce the M300 for ultra-large multimodal models next year. Management said broader Kunlunxin deployment should lower infrastructure costs and support AI Cloud Infra margins over time.
Advertising Pressure Remains the Main Challenge
Management expects online marketing revenue to remain under pressure from macroeconomic weakness, competition and Baidu’s AI search transition.

Baidu is prioritizing user experience over near-term monetization, which will weigh on revenue and profits in the near term. The company also expects continued investment in cloud infrastructure, chips and foundation models to limit near-term margin expansion.
However, management expects AI Cloud Infra to continue growing rapidly and increasingly offset advertising weakness over the medium to long term.
